problem.title: Kirby Problem 3.71
problem.statement:
Is there a nontrivial element in the kernel of the natural map

$$
\Theta^3_{\mathbb{Z}}\longrightarrow \Theta^3_{\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}};
$$

that is, does there exist an integer homology 3-sphere that does not bound a smooth $\mathbb{Z}$-homology 4-ball but does bound a smooth $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-homology 4-ball?
problem.background:
Source: Kirby's Problems in Low-Dimensional Topology notes. Original problem number: KP-3.71.

Literature notes:
There is a natural homomorphism from the concordance group $C$ to $\Theta^3_{\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}}$ via taking double branched covers. As discussed in Problem 3.72, $\Sigma(2,3,7)$ bounds a rational homology ball but, because its Rokhlin invariant is nontrivial, does not bound a $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-homology ball. See also [BL02] for some further discussion of $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-homology cobordism.

References cited:
- [BL02] Christian Bohr and Ronnie Lee. Homology cobordism and classical knot invariants. Comment. Math. Helv., 77(2):363–382, 2002. doi:10.1007/s00014-002-8344-0.

<!-- LITERATURE-TRIAGE:BEGIN -->
## Literature review (checked 2026-08-17)

**Status:** open  
**Classification:** OPEN-TRIAGE

**Current literature assessment.** No nontrivial kernel element from integral to mod-2 homology cobordism is known; familiar integral homology spheres bounding rational balls with Rokhlin invariant one cannot be examples.

**Verified partial progress.**

- Any smooth Z/2-homology ball is a rational homology ball, so the sought kernel sits inside the known nontrivial kernel of Theta^3_Z to Theta^3_Q.
- The converse fails as an inference: Sigma(2,3,7) bounds a rational ball but its nonzero Rokhlin invariant obstructs a Z/2-homology ball.
- Bohr--Lee provide mod-2 homology-cobordism constraints and relations to classical knot invariants, but no requested nonzero kernel class.

**Full solution or refutation.**

The question remains open; rational-ball examples with even-primary homology or nonzero Rokhlin invariant do not settle it.

**What remains.**

Construct a nontrivial integral homology sphere bounding a smooth mod-2 homology ball, likely with only odd torsion in the ball, or prove injectivity.

**Sources checked.**

- Baykur, Kirby, and Ruberman, K3 -- A New Problem List in Low-Dimensional Topology, Problem 3.71 (2026). (maintained_tracker): https://bpb-us-e2.wpmucdn.com/websites.umass.edu/dist/b/22144/files/2026/04/K3-problem-list-watermarked.pdf
  Evidence used: Retains the kernel question and explains why the standard Sigma(2,3,7) rational-ball example is not a mod-2 example.
- Christian Bohr and Ronnie Lee, Homology cobordism and classical knot invariants, Commentarii Mathematici Helvetici 77 (2002), 363--382. (primary): https://doi.org/10.1007/s00014-002-8344-0
  Evidence used: Develops constraints in Z/2-homology cobordism but does not produce the kernel element requested here.
- Ronald Fintushel and Ronald J. Stern, A mu-invariant one homology 3-sphere that bounds an orientable rational ball, Contemporary Mathematics 35 (1984), 265--268. (primary): https://doi.org/10.1090/conm/035/780582
  Evidence used: Provides the canonical rational-ball example whose nonzero Rokhlin invariant prevents it from answering the mod-2 question.

**Review notes.** Bounding a rational ball was not conflated with bounding a Z/2-homology ball.

This is a dated literature triage; an open classification is not proof that no later or unindexed result exists.
<!-- LITERATURE-TRIAGE:END -->
